web.title_en: CrossFit: Automated Discovery of Virtual Machine Callback Vulnerabilities via Contextual Link Analysis and Targeted Fuzzing
web.description_en: This paper introduces the CrossFit tool, which bridges the analytical gap between script language callbacks and native runtimes by combining static analysis with targeted fuzzing. It automatically uncovered 21 new memory safety vulnerabilities in PHP, Python, and Ruby. Its core innovation lies in leveraging contextual link analysis to precisely generate automated test cases that trigger complex callback side effects (e.g., use-after-free), significantly improving the efficiency of cross-language interaction vulnerability discovery.

web.description_en: This paper unveils Bit2Watt, a novel cross-layer vulnerability demonstrating how attackers can induce high-frequency power fluctuations solely by legitimately scheduling GPU workloads. web.title: An Abandoned CDN Domain Was Re-Registered. Thousands of Sites Still Call It.
web.description: In July 2025, someone registered a domain that used to belong to a content delivery network.  The CDN had been wound down years earlier, and the domain it served assets from was allowed to expire. What it had not lost were its callers. Thousands of websites, code repositories, and documentation pages still carry hard-coded references to hostnames beneath it.    The new owner holds wildcard DNS across the entire domain, and any hostname under it now resolves to infrastructure that person controls. Today the apex serves an ad-heavy media downloader page, which is unremarkable. The remarkable part is that the decision about what those thousands of pages load next belongs to a stranger, and nobody involved has been notified, because from the outside nothing broke.    This pattern is not hypothetical, and it's not unheard of either.
